title: Isoloom run manifest, version 0
description: What Isoloom writes next to one target's generated files (`.isoloom[-<n>]/<target>[/<cloud>]/run.json`) and the Isothrum runner executes. Declarative and deterministic: no secret values, no absolute paths, no timestamps, no host shell. Version 0 is unstable: Isoloom and the runner move together until 1.0.

manifest_version.description: The contract's version. 0: unstable, read only by a runner built for exactly 0.

generator.description: Provenance: a name and a version, nothing that changes between two runs of one Isoloom on one spec.

name.description: The spec's `name:`, with the instance suffix when there is one (`shop-2`): the default run name.

instance.description: The Isoloom instance the files were generated for (moved Docker blocks, `.isoloom-<n>/`), or null.

message.description: The spec's `message:`, its placeholders rewritten to manifest ones (`{{ machines.web.ports.0.publish }}` becomes `${published.web.80}`). The runner fills it once the run is ready; a sensitive output is never substituted.

cloud.description: The cloud of a cloud target's module; absent elsewhere.

driver.description: The runner driver that implements this manifest's actions, reads its status and clears its leftovers. The native commands themselves are in `lifecycle`.

hosts.description: Host operating systems this target runs from. A provider that exists on fewer (Hyper-V) narrows it in `identity.vagrant.providers`.

tools.description: The native tools the steps run, probed before `up`: a missing one fails with its name, not a raw spawn error.

params.description: Non-secret values set at run time that the generated files read (ISOLOOM_PUBLISH_ADDRESS, ISOLOOM_HYPERV_SWITCH, Terraform variables such as `region`).

secrets.description: Secret and input slots: names, sources and destinations, never values.

machines.description: Every machine the target creates, Isoloom's own included (`role` tells them apart): the runner never infers a role from a name, a label or an image.

ready.description: Conditions that must all hold, in order, once `lifecycle.up` succeeded, before the run counts as ready.

expiry.description: Runs that stop themselves (cloud auto-stop): the runner computes the expiry when it applies, passes it to the module, records it, and lists the run as expired after it (the reaper's input).

rel_path.description: Relative to the manifest's folder (or, where said, to the run's state folder), `/`-separated, never absolute, never escaping the lab. The runner converts separators for the host.

template.description: A string that may hold `${placeholder}`s (`$$` is a literal `$`). Roots: `run.name`, `run.dir` (the manifest's folder), `run.state_dir`, `run.provider`, `run.ssh_key`, `run.known_hosts`, `params.<NAME>`, `outputs.<name>`, `published.<machine>.<port>[.udp]`, `machine` (a per-machine step), `value` (an output's own `format`). There is no `secrets.` root: a secret reaches a tool only through its slot's delivery, so no value ever sits on a command line.

argv.description: A program and its arguments, run without a shell. The program is a bare tool name resolved on PATH (with its Windows wrapper when it has one). A shell is refused as the program: the manifest never holds shell code for the host.

host_argv.description: One argv for every host, or one per host OS (`default` covers the hosts not named). Only where a host truly differs.

probe.description: A read-only command that succeeds when the tool (and its daemon, for Docker) is usable. Time-bounded by the runner.

container.description: An image the runner may run the tool from instead of the host binary (Terraform for a LAN server from a macOS app). Pinned by digest.

identity.description: How the runner finds what this run created, without reading the generated files: the Compose project, the Vagrant folder and VM names, the Terraform module and state.

project.description: The project name: `${run.name}`, which the embedder may set (the launcher's `cyberctf-<lab id>`).

pinned_ports_file.description: The runner's override file of host ports pinned at the first start (in the run's state folder), named in every Compose argv. Always written, `services: {}` when nothing is pinned.

providers.description: The providers the Vagrantfile supports, each with the hosts it exists on, its plugin, and whether its commands need elevation.

elevation.description: `hyperv`: on Windows, management commands run elevated (one prompt per operation) when the runner may not manage Hyper-V itself. Status reads never are.

remote.description: The VMs run on a server (ESXi): its connection slots apply.

refusal.description: Why this lab can't run on this provider, in Isoloom's words (`refusal_on`), or null.

state.description: `runner`: local state in the run's state folder, outside the lab's files (a reinstalled lab must not orphan what it created).

var_files.description: Variable files Isoloom generated, in order (`terraform.tfvars.json`).

set_by.description: `runner`: the runner decides it (a relay's proxy command, the player's public IP). `embedder`: the app driving the runner passes it.

kind.description: `input`: a launch-time value of the lab (`inputs:`: a flag, a launch token). `secret`: the spec's `secrets:`. `connection`: what reaches the server or cloud account (a password, a token, keys). `generated`: made once per run by the runner and kept in its state.

sensitive.description: Masked in every event and log line. A flag, a token and a password always are.

machines.description: The machines (and their init jobs) that receive it.

source.description: Where the runner reads the value when the embedder passes none: one of Isoloom's secret stores, by reference.

delivery.description: Where a value goes. Never a command-line argument.

steps.description: The ids of the steps whose process gets it; `*` for every step of every operation.

shape.description: `string` (default): TF_VAR_<var>. `map_entry`: one key of a JSON-object variable (`inputs`), the runner writing the whole object.

path.description: Relative to the run's state folder; written owner-only, kept until `down` succeeded (a destroy needs the same values), named by `${run.state_dir}` in the steps that read it.

transport.description: Isoloom's guest delivery (`/var/lib/isoloom/secrets`, then `.delivered`): over SSH, `vagrant ssh`, or WinRM.

during_step.description: Delivered while this step runs (the guest waits for it), retried until it lands.

internet.description: false: no route out. On container targets Isoloom enforces it with `<machine>-routes` sidecars (role `infra`), not an `internal:` network, so published ports still work.

native.description: The network's name where the target creates it: the Docker network (`${run.name}_lab`), the hypervisor's internal network (`isoloom-<lab>-lab`).

role.description: `target`: part of the lab. `job`: a one-shot that must exit 0 (an `init:` script). `infra`: Isoloom's plumbing (the controller, probes, route keepers), never shown, never counted as down. `access`: the user's seat or its stand-in. `tool`: an observer (`tools:`). `check`: a check runner (Compose profile `check`).

of.description: The machine a job, route keeper or check runner belongs to.

addresses.description: Its static address on each lab network, by the lab's network name (what the status shows: no `docker inspect` needed).

native.description: Its name where the target creates it: the Compose service, or the VM name per provider (what orphan clean-up matches, exactly).

volumes.description: Named volumes, by the spec's name and mount path. `down` removes them; `park` and `resume` keep them (a flag written once by an init job lives in one).

publish.description: Published on the host. `ephemeral` (what the labs use): Docker picks the port unless ISOLOOM_PUBLISH_FIXED is set, and the runner pins it at the first start. `fixed`: always `preferred`.

keep_running.description: Infra that stays on once the lab is built (a controller with `keep_running`).

action.description: A driver primitive: a read-then-act sequence one argv can't express (list, then remove what was listed). The manifest's documentation fixes each action's native commands.

note.description: A line the runner emits when the step starts.

env.description: Non-secret environment of this step, values as templates (TF_DATA_DIR, TF_IN_AUTOMATION). Secrets and params come through their slots.

stdin.description: A generated file piped into the program (a check script into `docker compose exec -T <m> sh -s` or `ssh … sh -s`): the shell runs in the guest, never on the host.

when.description: `if_ok` (default): skipped once a step of the operation failed. `always`: a clean-up that runs anyway.

failure.description: `fail` (default) fails the operation; `tolerate` logs and goes on.

providers.description: Run only on these Vagrant providers (`${run.provider}`).

verdict.description: A regular expression over the step's lines; the last match leads the step's error (Ansible's `fatal: [host]: …`).

park.description: Absent: the run can't be parked (Terraform runs are created or destroyed). A mode absent inside it is refused.

resume.description: Brings parked machines back as they were. Never re-creates a container nor re-provisions a VM, so it needs no input again.

provision.description: Set-up again on running machines: `all`, or `machine` with `${machine}` bound.

status.description: The read-only probe the driver parses into machine states (an argv) or reads from files (an action). Never elevated, always time-bounded.

log.description: The bootstrap's log, whose tail explains a failure.

grammar.description: The file's first line: `ready`, `failed: <step>`, or `running: <step>`; anything else (or no file) means still booting.

via.description: A jump host (`user@host`), when the lab host sits behind one (a Proxmox node's internal bridge).

role.description: What the embedder does with it: `entry` (where to start: the Open button), `ssh` (the lab host's login), `address`, `credential`, `info`.

format.description: How the value is shown, `${value}` being the raw one (`http://127.0.0.1:${value}/`).

wait_s.description: How long the runner retries it before it fails (the spec's `wait`).

derived.description: Derived from the spec (reachability, no internet); skipped with ISOLOOM_DERIVED=0.

checks.description: The lab's checks, run by the runners Isoloom generated. Each runner prints `isoloom-check/1` lines; a check its runner never reported counts as failed.

protocol.description:
`isoloom-check: PASS `, `isoloom-check: FAIL : `, `isoloom-check: END

passed, failed`, matched anywhere in a line (a Vagrant or Compose prefix before it); the runner exits 0 only without a failure.

setup.description: Run before the runners (the access stand-ins; waking the controller).

from.description: Where it runs, for the report: `from the environment's networks`, `from web`, `inside web`.

step.description: Its `timeout_s` covers every check's `wait_s` plus a margin: a runner never stops before its slowest check could pass.

on_timeout.description: Clean-up after the runner ran out of time (its one-off container outlives the killed CLI).

teardown.description: Run after the runners, whatever happened.

recovery.description: A failed `up` that tripped over a previous run's leftovers, and how to clear them before one more try. A genuine failure is never retried.

stale_markers.description: Case-insensitive substrings of the failed step's output that mean leftovers, not a lab failure.

apply_retries.description: Terraform only: more applies after a failed one (a module that converges on a second apply, `cloud.apply_retries`).
